tools.title: Airtable

servers.name: Airtable MCP server
servers.capabilities: List and search bases, change schema, read, create and update records, comment, manage disabled automations, within the user's permissions.

tools.notes: All plans; calls count against Airtable API rate limits. Personal access tokens are the alternative to OAuth for CLI and server-side use.

tools.title: Apache Spark
tools.summary: Distributed engine for large-scale data processing, SQL, streaming and machine learning.

servers.name: MCP Server for Apache Spark History Server
servers.capabilities: Inspect applications, jobs, stages, executors, SQL plans and environment of a Spark History Server, compare runs and investigate failures; guided prompts.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

tools.notes: No MCP server from the Apache Spark project found on 2026-11-24 (spark.apache.org). The registered server is a Kubeflow project: set SHS_MCP__TRANSPORT=stdio and SHS_SERVERS__LOCAL__URL to the History Server URL (default http://localhost:18080); a History Server behind authentication also reads SHS_SERVERS__LOCAL__AUTH__USERNAME, __PASSWORD or __TOKEN, or a config.yaml passed with --config.

tools.title: BigQuery

servers.name: BigQuery remote MCP server
servers.capabilities: List datasets and tables, read schemas and run SQL queries in BigQuery.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: Enabled with the BigQuery API; the user needs the MCP Tool User, BigQuery Job User and BigQuery Data Viewer roles. Auth is OAuth 2.0 with IAM.

tools.title: Contentful

servers.name: Contentful Remote MCP
servers.capabilities: Manage entries, assets, content types and environments with the user's Contentful permissions.

servers.name: Contentful MCP server (local)
servers.capabilities: Same content management tools run locally with a Management API token.

tools.notes: The MCP app must be installed in each space/environment before the remote server works. EU organizations use https://mcp.eu.contentful.com/mcp. GA per Contentful's blog of 21 July 2026.

tools.title: Databricks
tools.summary: Data and AI platform (lakehouse, SQL warehouses, Unity Catalog).

servers.name: Databricks Unity Gateway MCP: system.ai.genie_one_mcp

settings.name: workspace_host
settings.description: Databricks: your workspace host, without https://

servers.capabilities: Ask questions over governed data through Genie from an MCP client.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

servers.name: Databricks Unity Gateway MCP: system.ai.dbsql

settings.name: workspace_host
settings.description: Databricks: your workspace host, without https://

servers.capabilities: Run SQL on Databricks SQL warehouses.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: Uses the ai-gateway OAuth scope; Beta servers need an account admin to enable the Enhanced Unity Gateway preview. Workspace endpoints under /api/2.0/mcp/ (Genie, AI Search, UC functions) are Public Preview.

tools.title: dbt
tools.summary: Data transformation framework (dbt Core, Fusion and the dbt platform).

servers.name: dbt MCP Server (local)
servers.capabilities: Run dbt CLI commands, query the Semantic Layer, Discovery and Admin APIs, and execute or generate SQL.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

servers.name: dbt MCP Server (remote)

settings.name: dbt_host
settings.description: dbt: your dbt host, without https://

servers.capabilities: Hosted dbt MCP on the dbt platform: Semantic Layer, Discovery and SQL tools without local install.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: Local: DBT_PROJECT_DIR and DBT_PATH for CLI tools; DBT_HOST, DBT_TOKEN, DBT_PROD_ENV_ID for dbt platform features. Remote OAuth is public beta (Starter, Enterprise, Enterprise+); token auth needs the x-dbt-prod-environment-id header.

tools.title: MongoDB
tools.summary: Document database, self-managed or MongoDB Atlas.

servers.name: MongoDB Atlas Managed MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Query and manage Atlas clusters, databases and collections with OAuth sign-in.

servers.name: MongoDB MCP Server (local)
servers.capabilities: Connect to MongoDB deployments and query data and metadata. The registered invocation sets --readOnly.
servers.scopes: Database or Atlas roles held by the supplied credentials. Consent: Supply a MongoDB connection string or Atlas service account credentials for the intended deployment.

read_only.how: The registered command starts the server with --readOnly: only read tools are exposed.

tools.notes: The remote managed server cannot be used with a static API key over HTTP; clients without OAuth use the mongodb-atlas-mcp-remote stdio package with service-account credentials. --readOnly is the documented default example.

tools.title: Neon

servers.name: Neon MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Manage projects, branches and compute endpoints, run SQL and inspect schemas; ?readonly=true and category filters available.
servers.scopes: Projects and operations accessible to the authorized identity. Consent: Approve the Neon OAuth request or supply an authorized Neon API key.

read_only.how: The endpoint https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp?readonly=true exposes only read tools.

tools.notes: API-key auth sends a Neon API key as Bearer token. Observability tools need the Neon Platform Beta (aws-us-east-2 only).

tools.title: PostgreSQL

servers.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases (PostgreSQL prebuilt)
servers.capabilities: Explore schemas and run SQL against any PostgreSQL database with prebuilt tools.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: PostgreSQL has no vendor MCP server. This one is published by Google (about 16,900 stars, active), so it counts as community for PostgreSQL; database user/password are credentials, so use a dedicated least-privilege role. The archived reference server from modelcontextprotocol/servers should not be used.

tools.title: Redis
tools.summary: In-memory data store, cache and vector database.

servers.name: Redis MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Read and write Redis data structures (strings, hashes, lists, sets, streams, JSON) and run vector search.

tools.notes: Connection can be given as --url or through the REDIS_* environment variables (TLS and Entra ID variables also supported).

tools.title: Sanity
tools.summary: Headless content platform with structured content and GROQ queries.

servers.name: Sanity MCP server
servers.capabilities: Content operations, GROQ queries, schema exploration and deployment, releases, datasets and project management.

tools.notes: GA status is from Sanity's v2.6.0 changelog (11 Dec 2025). A Bearer API token in the Authorization header replaces OAuth; image generation tools consume AI credits.

tools.title: Segment
tools.summary: Customer data platform for collecting and routing events.
tools.notes: No Segment MCP server for workspace data found on 2026-11-21; use the Segment Public API. Twilio's docs-only server (https://mcp.twilio.com/docs, public beta) searches Segment documentation.

tools.title: Snowflake

servers.name: Snowflake-managed MCP Server

settings.name: account_host
settings.description: Snowflake: your account host, without https://

servers.capabilities: Expose Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Cortex Agents, SQL execution and custom tools defined on an MCP server object.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: An MCP server object must be created in Snowflake first (role needs USAGE on it). Auth by Snowflake OAuth (no dynamic registration) or a programmatic access token as Bearer. The Snowflake-Labs/mcp server is deprecated and archived.

tools.title: Strapi

servers.name: Strapi MCP server (built in)
servers.capabilities: Manage content of a Strapi instance with an admin token's permissions.

tools.notes: Self-hosted: served at /mcp on your own Strapi (localhost URL is the docs' example). Needs Strapi 5.47.0+, mcp.enabled: true in config/server, and an Admin token as Authorization: Bearer.

tools.title: Supabase
tools.summary: Postgres development platform with auth, storage and edge functions.

servers.name: Supabase MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Manage tables, run SQL, fetch config, logs and docs for Supabase projects; can be scoped with project_ref, read_only and features parameters.
servers.scopes: Authorized organization, subject to any project_ref and features filters. Consent: Sign in to Supabase and authorize access to the intended organization.

read_only.how: The endpoint https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?read_only=true exposes only read tools and runs SQL as a read-only Postgres role; project_ref and features filters still apply.

tools.notes: Local Supabase CLI exposes http://localhost:54321/mcp and self-hosted instances offer a limited tool subset without OAuth.
